newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha falls below $200/tonne - traders.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha falls below $200/tonne - traders.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices fell below $200 per tonne in early afternoon trade on Thursday, oil product traders said.
It is the first time near-term naphtha prices have fallen below $200 since September 1996, they said.
Prompt second-half August open-spec naphtha fell by $3.00 per tonne to $199.00/$200.00 in Thursday afternoon trade from about $202.00/203.00 on Wednesday.
"There are quite a few traders offering second-half August cargoes at $200.00 with no firm bids," one naphtha trader said.
Traders attributed the decline in naphtha prices to an overnight tumble in crude oil prices overseas and weaker European naphtha markets.

Traders also said that it was too early to tell when and at what level naphtha prices would rebound, but that some end-users were certain to emerge in the market soon to hunt for bargains, effectively buttressing market sentiment.
Asia's benchmark open-spec naphtha prices have largely been declining since early January, when prompt naphtha levels hit $252.00 per tonne, due to weaker global crude oil markets.
An inflow of European and African cargoes into Asia also put downward pressure on the regional market, traders said.
